title: Turn-hybrid continuous batcher: KV sparse reclamation & slab consolidation
creator: Diego Morales
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts with long responses and vice versa, interleaved by user sessions) are causing KV cache fragmentation and GPU memory pressure. The current continuous batcher keeps per-request KV residency conservatively, which preserves quality but leads to high memory footprint and increased OOM risk during bursty long-response tails. Goal: reduce steady-state KV footprint without increasing tail latency or breaking correctness of cached KV for active dialogs.
proposed_approach: Introduce a turn-hybrid reclamation policy that combines: 1) sparse reclamation: probabilistically evict low-access KV shards (LRU + access-frequency bloom) under sustained pressure rather than wholesale per-slot eviction; 2) slab consolidation: periodically compact small KV slabs belonging to the same model/session into contiguous allocations and free underutilized fragments; 3) per-turn reservation quotas: reserve a small token budget per active conversation to prevent premature eviction during an in-flight response; 4) compressed cold pages: move older, rarely-accessed KV segments to quantized/FP16 compressed backup pages kept in GPU if bandwidth allows or host pinned memory as fallback. The batcher will expose two knobs: pressure_threshold (nvml mem percent) and sparse_eviction_rate (probability mass).
acceptance_criteria: 1) 25% reduction in median GPU KV memory footprint across mixed-turn benchmark (see links) without >5% increase in p95 latency for token generation. 2) No regression in sampled quality metrics (per-turn perplexity and safety checks) from baseline. 3) Failover path (host-pinned KV) increases inference latency <10ms on average when used. 4) Automated canary rollout and rollback hooks implemented in runtime with observability dashboards.
design_decisions: - Use frequency-sketch (Count-Min with decay) to approximate access hotness rather than per-entry exact counters to bound memory overhead. - Prioritize reclaiming shards with low recent access and high fragmentation score computed from slab metadata. - Do not evict entries that were written in the last N tokens of a conversation (turn sticky window), N default 64. - Compress only when GPU memory pressure crosses pressure_threshold to avoid extra CPU/GPU cycles at steady state.
tradeoffs: - Pros: Lower steady memory use, fewer OOM incidents, better packing of batches allowing higher throughput. - Cons: Extra complexity in allocator/GC, added CPU work for compaction/compression cycles, small risk of cache misses leading to KV rebuilds. Mitigation: conservative defaults and staged rollouts.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (experimental): Implement frequency sketch and sparse eviction prototype gated behind runtime flag. Hook nvml-based mem watchers, add metrics for eviction count, rebuilt_kv_events, and compaction_time. Phase 2 (bench): Run mixed-turn harness (short-long interleaved) on dedicated cluster nodes, collect mem/latency/quality. Phase 3 (canary): Enable default sparse_eviction_rate=0.02 on 1% of traffic, enable dashboards and automated rollback. Phase 4 (gradual ramp): Increase to 10%/50% and tune thresholds, then GA when SLOs met.
benchmarks_and_results: (experiment logs) 2026-02-24: baseline run (v2.3) over 24h mixed-turn workload: median KV mem 9.7GB, p95 token latency 48ms. 2026-03-02: sparse eviction prototype run: median KV mem 7.1GB (-27%), p95 latency 49.8ms (+3.7%). Rebuild_rate: 0.8% of requests caused a KV rebuild; quality checks unchanged on sampled evals. Compaction CPU overhead avg 6% on controller threads during maintenance windows. Detailed benchmark artifacts: https://redwood-internal/bench/turn-hybrid/2026-03-02
rollout_plan: - Canary endpoint rollout (1% traffic) for 72 hours with heightened telemetry. - Automated guardrails: if rebuilt_kv_rate > 3% OR p95 latency regression > 10% for 10m, auto-disable. - Phased ramp to 10% -> 50% -> 100% across 2 weeks. - Post-mortem checklist for OOMs and user reports.
monitoring_and_metrics: Add new charts: kv_memory_residency_by_model, slab_fragmentation_index, evictions_per_minute, rebuilt_kv_rate, compaction_cpu_pct, compressed_pages_count. Alert rules: kv_memory_residency > 85% of node capacity for 5m; rebuilt_kv_rate > 2% sustained for 10m.
safety_and_fallbacks: - Per-request routing: if runtime observes >90% memory pressure, route new requests to compressed-kv-compatible model variant or lower-memory quantized model. - If canary triggers rollback, runtime must preserve request-level correctness: restored entries are re-populated lazily. - Add deterministic logging for any skipped eviction that would have violated turn sticky window for debugging.
dependencies_notes: Blocks work in allocator refactor (ENG-361210) for slab metadata headers. Relies on slot-coalescing improvements in ENG-412005 to reduce fragmentation after compaction.
